Female (n=10): body 2.5-2.8 mm; fore coxa yellow; basal radial vein haired and hind tibia entirely darkened (separating from S. maklarini and S. cheedhangi); cibarium with 75 minute processes; claw with small subbasal tooth; sternite 7 with large sternal plate. Pupa (n=25): 2.7-3.6 mm; head bare except medial area around facial trichomes covered with tubercles (absent in S. maklarini); 6 gill filaments (2+2+2, 0.7-1.4 mm) with sharply edged reticulate annular ridges; no terminal hooks; shoe-shaped cocoon (3.2-3.7 x 1.2-1.5 mm). Mature larva (n=7): 4.5-5.2 mm; antennal segments 1.00:1.15-1.19:0.65-0.73 (vs 0.95-0.98 for 2nd/1st in S. cheedhangi); labral fan 40-41 rays; postgenal cleft 3.0-3.3x bridge; posterior circlet 84-90 rows (vs 115-170 in S. laterale).

Female (body 2.6 mm, wing 2.5 mm): 5-vittate scutum, simple claws, all femora entirely yellow (apex of hind femur slightly darkened; much paler than S. chaliowae and S. chainarongi), sensory vesicle 0.36x 3rd palpal segment, sternite 8 with 32-36 stout hairs/side, genital fork arms with wide plate-like anterior projection. Male unknown in 1999 and 2004. Pupa (2.8 mm): 8 short paired subequal gill filaments (1.0-0.6 mm, 140 deg angle, dorsalmost 1.3x ventralmost), thoracic trichomes more branched (4-5 branches mediodorsally) than S. chaliowae/S. chainarongi; corbicular shoe-shaped cocoon roughly woven anteriorly with large and small open spaces in anterior collar. Larva (5.4-6.0 mm): lacking abdominal protuberances; labral fan 56-60 rays; hypostomal teeth apically rounded; postgenal cleft rounded anteriorly, ca. 2.0x postgenal bridge; rectal gill 10-13 lobules/lobe; posterior circlet 112-134 rows of up to 22 hooklets (Takaoka & Kuvangkadilok 1999 pp. 504-507; Takaoka & Choochote 2004 pp. 194-197).
